doc_friction.issue: Says 'Not yet: the deploy workflow' on main although #19617 ported it and it already ran once (45947552522); the run's failure was found only through the Actions API, not any file.
The token row lists R2 edit as required, but the repository token has none; nothing in the tree records which permissions the shared token actually holds.
PR #19625 was titled as a workflow port when I checked, then retitled after it took the same R2 fix; a title search cannot catch duplicates that change scope mid-flight.

Three sessions fixed the same two deploy blockers within an hour; nothing claims a failed deploy run, so every watcher of payapps-deploy races to fix it. A claim branch per failing run id (like security-fix/*) would stop it.

notes: Bet #1. First deploy (run 45947552522) failed on R2 auth; I patched provision.mjs, but PR #19625 landed the same fix first and run 45949861746 deployed PayApps (Free plan, no attachments) to https://payapps.duncan-andrew-haywood.workers.dev, smoke test passed. My duplicate was resolved to main's version. The next dispatch (45950799211) stopped on a race in the SOV import: useMutation's mutationFn read `result` from a stale closure ('Nothing to import' shown beside the preview). Fixed by passing the input as the mutation argument. Unit suite 1286 passed, typecheck and biome clean. 12 parallel loaded runs did not reproduce the race on the old code; the failed run's DOM is the evidence. Follow-up: other components may close over state in mutationFn the same way. Superseded twice: PR #19625 landed the R2 fix and PR #19639 the save-mutation fix while this PR waited on CI. What this PR still adds: the copy-from-another-job mutation takes its job id and amounts toggle as arguments (the same stale-closure class #19639 left in place).

human_equivalent.basis: diagnose two deploy failures, fix provisioning fallback and a React Query stale-closure race

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
